ai_policy.summary: Journal instructions contemplate generated manuscript text and research data analysis under disclosure and human accountability; explicit analysis permission covers analytical code in this workflow.

disclosure.instructions: Declare generated text in acknowledgements or footnote, data collection or analysis in Methods, generated visuals in captions; describe tool name/version, use, dates and access as reasonably possible, and third-party citations. The journal additionally requires assistance in drafting manuscripts to be noted in both the cover letter and acknowledgements, with authors declaring full responsibility for scientific content.

restrictions: Authors remain accountable, verify outputs and references, and must not list AI as an author.

policy_sources.note: Journal author instructions cover generated text and collecting or analyzing data with disclosure.

ai_policy.summary: Publisher permits bounded research, basic analysis and substantive drafting with human oversight; journal-specific application requires confirmation. The journal itself additionally requires a title-page footnote about AI use during submission.

disclosure.instructions: Describe research use in Methods; add an end-of-paper AI Use Declaration detailing manuscript preparation and human accountability. Guidance requests tool versions, dates, prompts and extent. Journal-specific instructions additionally require disclosure during submission in a brief title-page footnote describing how and for what purposes AI was used.
disclosure.section: How can authors use AIGC? Core principles

restrictions: AI may assist basic analysis and literature-review or summary drafting; humans verify outputs and retain interpretation and original scientific thinking. AI must not write the entire manuscript or interpret data.
Publisher guidance read; journal-specific restrictions have not been independently ruled out.

policy_sources.applicability: Publisher policy; journal-specific application or exceptions need confirmation
policy_sources.note: Guidance explicitly permits literature assistance, basic analysis, and literature-review or summary drafting with oversight.
Requires title-page footnote and submission disclosure for drafting, editing, data analysis, or theoretical proof development or verification; this disclosure alone is not affirmative permission.

patches.audit_note: Reviewed merged fee, geography, AI policy and retained metrics; unchanged fields remain with role audits. Metrics not independently reverified are retained with their prior evidence and limitations.

findings.issue: Existing AI disclosure instructions omit a separate journal instruction requiring disclosure of drafting assistance in the cover letter and acknowledgements.
findings.resolution: Added the journal-specific instruction while retaining other disclosure requirements.

findings.issue: The journal homepage supplies a specific title-page footnote disclosure requirement missing from publisher-only guidance.
findings.resolution: Added journal-specific disclosure; compatibility remains unclear pending confirmation of applicable substantive permission.

notes: Reviewed all 18 merged candidates; official Springer journal homepages independently checked for current 2025 citation metrics for Policy Sciences, Public Organization Review, Public Choice and International Tax and Public Finance. Other retained metrics rely on preceding audits; some Taylor & Francis values derive from search-indexed content with direct access blocked.

Reviewed fee and geography audit claims for completeness and internal contradictions; no independent claim of a comprehensive re-audit of each source. Fee eligibility remains conditional or unverified where evidence is incomplete. Journal citation metrics do not indicate acceptance likelihood.

Cambridge public-policy author instructions and Springer publisher AI guidance and International Tax and Public Finance journal homepage independently read. AI compatibility and author eligibility are not inferred from mere silence.
